title: SubtreeLU: High-Performance Parallel Sparse LU Factorization for Circuit Simulation
problem: Parallel sparse LU factorization for circuit simulation faces synchronization overheads, conservative dependency estimation, and under-utilization of supernodal structures in existing SPICE solvers.
motivation: Solving sparse linear systems via LU factorization is a critical performance bottleneck in SPICE-based circuit simulation.
method: SubtreeLU reshapes the separator tree—the structure that nested dissection creates from circuit equations—by combining or splitting pieces to form a private-pipeline where processors work independently without synchronizing. It supports both pivoting (reordering values for numerical stability) and non-pivoting modes. Supernodal methods batch related operations together to speed up the numerical calculations.
key_novelty: Reorganizing the separator tree into a private-pipeline structure that decouples synchronization constraints, allowing processors to work independently in parallel sparse LU factorization.
contributions: Novel scheduling framework for organizing computation into private-pipeline structures that eliminate synchronization bottlenecks
Support for both pivoting and non-pivoting modes in a unified framework
Supernodal method integration for improved numerical update acceleration
Consistent improvements in accuracy, runtime, and scalability on 46 circuit matrices versus NICSLU and CKTSO

metrics.speedup: Outperforms NICSLU and CKTSO on runtime

limitations: Evaluation focused on 46 circuit matrices; generalization to other sparse linear system solvers not addressed.
